newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Western Australian power restrictions lifted.
newsitem.headline: Western Australian power restrictions lifted.

text.p: Power restrictions affecting about 700,000 consumers in the south-west of Western Australia were lifted late Monday night, Western Power Corp said on Tuesday.

A Western Power spokesman said the six-day old restrictions were lifted after coal plant operators at Muja Power station returned to work early on Monday morning and last minute bans by Muja station controllers were lifted on Monday night.
The south-west grid, which includes Perth and parts of the Kalgoorlie gold belt, had been restored its full 2,800 megawatt capacity.

The industrial action was part of an on-going campaign co-ordinated by Western Australia's peak union organisation, the Trades and Labour Council (TLC), against proposed changes to the state's industrial relations laws, including compulsory pre-strike secret ballots.
Western Australia accounts for about 10 percent of Australia's economic output, with all of the nation's iron ore mining from the northwest Pilbara and most of the gold production.
The state government on Monday announced a package of amendments based on a TLC submission handed to them late last week.
However, TLC secretary Tony Cooke said on Tuesday more changes were necessary and the campaign would continue, with a 24-hour stoppage planned in the manufacturing sector next week.
"(The campaign) continues and not just in one industry," Cooke said on Australian Broadcasting Corp Radio.
"Across the construction industry there is continuing action in place and it has been in place for some time," he said.
